chunks: And Jahm ibn Abī Jahm narrated, saying:

I saw Abā al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, and he had performed sajdah after the three rakʿahs of Maghrib. So I said to him, “May I be your ransom, I saw you prostrate after the three [rakʿahs].” He said, “And you saw me?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “Then do not abandon it, for du'a in it is answered.”

key_terms.الرَّكَعَاتِ: the units of salat (prayer), here referring to the three rakʿahs of Maghrib
key_terms.فَلَا تَدَعْهَا: do not leave it or abandon it

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام say about making sajdah after Maghrib prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام performed a sajdah after the three rakʿahs of Maghrib and instructed that it should not be abandoned. It indicates the merit of this prostration and highlights that du'a made in it is answered.
